items.title: Embracing the Bond Market: Masters in Business with Robin Wigglesworth
items.content: <article>Barry speaks with Robin Wigglesworth, editor of Financial Times' Alphaville blog and author of the new book 'A Fabulous Debt: The Epic Story of How Bonds Built the Modern World'. They discuss the bond market as the engine of the global economy, why the 30-year mortgage is "a miracle of the modern world," and when we should actually start worrying about US debt. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: French Protesters Dispersed with Gas as Tensions Rise
items.content: <article>Student protesters in Paris, France were dispersed with gas as conflict escalates.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: New Middle East Threats, Russian Diesel Coming to US
items.content: <article>The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by The New Yorker Staff Writer Gideon Lewis-Kraus, Linx Dating Founder & CEO Amy Andersen, Oliver Wyman Geostrategy Practice Partner & Global Head Daniel Tannebaum, Seaport Research Partners Chief Equity Strategist Jonathan Golub, SHRM President and CEO Johnny C. Taylor Jr, The Wall Street Journal Foreign Correspondent and “This Cursed Beautiful Land” Author Evan Gershkovich, The Atlantic CEO and “The Running Ground” Author Nicholas Thompson and “Sleuth-Hound” Author Lindsey Fitzharris. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: ‘Total Meltdown’ in Riskiest Debt Unnerves Market: Credit Weekly
items.author: Aaron Weinman, Josie Reich and Paula Sambo
items.content: <article>It was a panicked message from a colleague that woke fund manager Ivelina Green at 5 a.m. on Thursday morning in New York: “Total meltdown.”</article>

items.title: Metals Traders Reap Bonanza With Another Year of Record Profits
items.author: Jack Farchy, Archie Hunter and Alfred Cang
items.content: <article>Metals traders are earning billions of dollars in a second consecutive blowout year for the sector, with several top trading houses notching up record profits.</article>

items.title: The Real Medical Detective Who Inspired Sherlock Holmes
items.content: <article>Medical historian Lindsey Fitzharris tells Bloomberg This Weekend how Scottish surgeon Joseph Bell’s remarkable powers of observation inspired his student Arthur Conan Doyle to create Sherlock Holmes. Speaking with hosts Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo, Fitzharris discusses her new book, Sleuth-Hound: The Case of the Real Sherlock Holmes, and Bell’s largely forgotten work applying his diagnostic skills to real criminal investigations. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Venezuela to Restart a Crucial Power Plant With China’s Help
items.author: Patricia Garip and Fabiola Zerpa
items.content: <article>A Chinese engineering company is on the cusp of partially restarting a massive Venezuelan power plant that’s been largely idle for years, a crucial step toward fixing the nation’s dilapidated grid.</article>

items.title: Dalmore Said to Express Interest in Cinven-Owned UK Supplier JLA
items.author: Crystal Tse and Swetha Gopinath
items.content: <article>Dalmore Capital is among parties that have expressed interest in acquiring UK commercial equipment supplier and services provider JLA Group from buyout firm Cinven, according to people with knowledge of the matter.</article>

items.title: How This County Made the Data Center Boom Pay Off
items.content: <article>AI is driving a wave of new data centers, but communities are increasingly asking what they get in return. Virginia’s Loudoun County turned the industry into a major tax base that helped fund schools, parks and infrastructure, yet even there, officials are now putting limits on further growth. The bigger lesson may be that towns have more bargaining power than they think. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Inside Gershkovich’s 16 Months in Russian Prisons
items.content: <article>Wall Street Journal foreign correspondent Evan Gershkovich tells Bloomberg This Weekend how his reporting experience and knowledge of Russia helped him understand that his 2023 arrest on false espionage charges was likely intended to make him part of a prisoner exchange. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Gershkovich discusses his 16 months in Russian prisons, his memoir This Cursed Beautiful Land and what Stephen Hubbard’s release says about Moscow’s use of detained Americans in its dealings with Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
items.content: <article>Modern day apple-picking, country clubs getting more fun, AirBnB rules update, and The The Brewers' playoff anthem: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: HR Navigates AI and a Changing Workplace
items.content: <article>SHRM President and CEO Johnny C. Taylor Jr. tells Bloomberg This Weekend how employers and workers can navigate open enrollment, AI-driven job disruption and growing generational divides in the workplace. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Taylor says companies need to communicate more clearly about benefits, help employees understand how AI can complement human intelligence and teach workers how to disagree constructively. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Persistent Oil Prices Threaten Inflation Outlook
items.content: <article>Seaport Research Partners Chief Equity Strategist Jonathan Golub tells Bloomberg This Weekend that stocks are not in an AI bubble, arguing that strong earnings and lower valuations show investors remain skeptical even as AI drives much of the market. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Golub says a prolonged Middle East conflict could keep oil and inflation elevated, eventually forcing the Federal Reserve to respond as strains emerge in credit markets. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Russian Diesel Deal Confronts Legal Uncertainty
items.content: <article>Oliver Wyman Geostrategy Practice Leader Daniel Tannebaum tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the first Russian diesel shipment under President Donald Trump’s deal with Vladimir Putin raises legal and compliance questions while offering limited relief for US fuel prices. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Tannebaum says private companies remain wary of doing business with Russia and warns that uncertainty over US sanctions and technology policy could push foreign governments and businesses toward alternatives to American suppliers. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: France Faces New Protests After Week of Violence
items.content: <article>Bloomberg News Paris Deputy Bureau Chief James Regan tells Bloomberg This Weekend that France is deploying tens of thousands of police and shifting protest routes as authorities try to prevent a repeat of last weekend’s violence and looting. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Regan says unrest that began with student demands has broadened into anger over the cost of living, threatening retailers and tourism as France also contends with fiscal and political strains. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Gershkovich Says Putin Seeks His Terms, Not a Deal
items.content: <article>Wall Street Journal foreign correspondent Evan Gershkovich tells Bloomberg This Weekend that he questions whether the Trump administration fully understands Vladimir Putin’s negotiating tactics after US envoy Steve Witkoff praised the Russian president as a “humanitarian” following Stephen Hubbard’s release. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Gershkovich draws on years covering Putin and his own 16 months in Russian custody to argue that the Russian leader remains focused on securing his demands for Ukraine rather than compromising in negotiations. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Oil Markets Brace for Renewed Iran Fighting
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Economics Chief Emerging Markets Economist Ziad Daoud tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the risk of renewed fighting between the US, Israel and Iran is rising, helping keep oil prices elevated even as energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz recover. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Daoud says the conflict could remain a long-term stalemate, with heightened shipping costs, depleted stockpiles and escalating regional tensions continuing to threaten global energy supplies. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Barclays ‘House of Fixed Income’ Pins Future Growth on Equities
items.author: William Shaw
items.content: <article>The house built by fixed income is facing an overhaul. Barclays Plc is showing it can do more for clients than trade bonds and arrange debt deals.</article>

items.title: Indonesia Begins Trimming Pipeline Gas Exports to Singapore
items.author: Ben Otto
items.content: <article>Indonesia is reducing natural gas exports to neighboring Singapore as President Prabowo Subianto seeks to shore up domestic supply and strengthen energy security for Southeast Asia’s largest economy.</article>

items.title: Kenya Records Second Ebola Death as Uganda Restricts Transit
items.author: Helen Nyambura
items.content: <article>Kenya has reported a second death from Ebola, a 65-year-old woman who was a close family member of the index case, while Uganda said it’s restricting transit for anyone with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of the Congo in an effort to halt the disease spreading.</article>
